sub: Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy · c. 1450–1400 BC

stops.before: Joseph is forgotten. The Israelites have multiplied into a nation of slaves, and Pharaoh has ordered their baby boys drowned in the Nile.
stops.watch: Two midwives who fear God more than the king; a mother who hides her son three months, then sets him afloat; Pharaoh's daughter who names him 'drawn out'. Forty years later, a murder, a flight to Midian, a well and a wife — and God 'remembers his covenant'.
stops.after: At the back of the desert, a bush that burns and is not consumed.

stops.before: Moses is eighty, a shepherd for his father-in-law, far from Egypt and from any thought of his people.
stops.watch: 'Put off the shoes from thy feet.' God gives his name — the name so holy the Jews will not say it — and Moses gives five excuses, each answered. Aaron becomes his mouth. The first audience with Pharaoh goes badly: 'Who is the Lord, that I should hear his voice?'
stops.after: Pharaoh has said no. God begins to take Egypt apart.

stops.before: Egypt is the greatest power on earth and its gods rule the river, the sun and the harvest. Each plague strikes one of them.
stops.watch: Blood, frogs, gnats, flies, cattle, boils, hail, locusts, darkness — and Pharaoh's heart, which he hardens and God hardens, alternately. Between each plague the tension is the same sentence: 'Let my people go.' The tenth is announced in chapter 11 and falls in the next stop.
stops.after: On the night of the tenth plague, the meal that Israel will eat for ever.

stops.before: Every house in Egypt will lose its firstborn tonight — unless its doorposts are marked with the blood of a lamb.
stops.watch: The lamb, the unleavened bread, the girded loins: the Passover, which is also the Last Supper's shape. The night flight, the pillar of cloud and fire, the sea standing up in walls, and Miriam's song on the far shore — the oldest poem in the Bible.
stops.after: Free, and in a desert with nothing to eat.

stops.before: Three days from the sea the water is bitter and the people already wish they had died in Egypt.
stops.watch: Manna — 'what is it?' — every morning except the Sabbath, and quail in the evening; water from the rock at Horeb; the first battle, won while Moses' arms are held up; and Jethro's advice that Moses cannot judge everyone alone. Watch the murmuring: it is the pattern of the next forty years.
stops.after: In the third month they come to the mountain, and God comes down.

stops.before: Israel camps at the foot of Sinai. God offers them something no nation has been offered: to be his own people, a kingdom of priests.
stops.watch: The Ten Words spoken out of fire and smoke while the people beg Moses to hear them instead; then the 'book of the covenant' — laws about slaves, oxen, widows and strangers — and the blood sprinkled on the people. Chapter 24 ends with seventy elders eating and drinking in the sight of God.
stops.after: Moses goes up the mountain for forty days to receive the plan of a tent.

stops.before: God will travel with his people. He describes, cubit by cubit, the tent he will live in, and the clothes his priest will wear.
stops.watch: Read with the diagrams open: the Ark and the mercy seat, the table, the lampstand, the curtains, the altar — everything moving inward toward one room. Chapter 28 dresses Aaron: the twelve stones over his heart and 'Holy to the Lord' on his forehead.
stops.after: While Moses is still on the mountain, the people below make a god they can see.

stops.before: Forty days is too long. The people ask Aaron for gods to go before them, and he makes one from their earrings.
stops.watch: Moses arguing God out of destroying Israel, then smashing the tablets himself; the Levites' terrible zeal; and the greatest conversation in the Old Testament — 'Show me thy glory' — answered by God passing by and naming himself 'merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion'. Moses comes down with his face shining.
stops.after: Forgiven, the people build the tent exactly as it was shown.

stops.before: The people who gave gold for a calf now give so much for the Tabernacle that Moses has to tell them to stop.
stops.watch: Bezalel and Oholiab, the first artists filled with the Spirit of God. Then, on the first day of the first month of the second year, the tent goes up and the cloud comes down — and Moses himself cannot enter. Exodus ends with God living in the middle of the camp.
stops.after: A God this close needs rules for approaching him: Leviticus.

stops.before: The tent is built and the priests are ready. Leviticus is the manual — and the book where most readers give up. Take the doors that open onto the story.
stops.watch: Chapter 1 shows what a sacrifice was; 8–10 ordain Aaron, and two of his sons die for offering 'strange fire'; 16 is the Day of Atonement, the one day the high priest passes the veil; 19 holds 'thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself'. The rest is there when you want it.
stops.after: The camp is counted, ordered, and set marching.

stops.t: Grapes of Canaan, forty years of sand
stops.before: Eleven days from Sinai to the edge of the promised land. Twelve spies go in and come back with a cluster of grapes so big two men carry it — and with fear.
stops.watch: The people refuse to go up, and God turns them round for forty years until that generation dies. Korah's rebellion and the earth opening; Aaron's rod that buds; Moses striking the rock in anger and losing the land himself; the bronze serpent on a pole that Jesus will compare himself to.
stops.after: On the plains of Moab a pagan prophet is hired to curse Israel.

stops.before: Israel is camped across the Jordan from Jericho, and the king of Moab is terrified.
stops.watch: The prophet who cannot say what he is paid to say, the donkey who sees the angel first, and the oracle that looks past Moab's day: 'A star shall rise out of Jacob.' In chapter 27 Moses climbs a mountain to see the land, and lays hands on Joshua.
stops.after: Moses, a hundred and twenty years old, turns to the people for three last speeches.

stops.before: Deuteronomy is Moses' farewell: the whole story retold to the children of those who left Egypt, on the last day of his life.
stops.watch: The Ten Commandments again, then the sentence every Jew still prays twice a day: 'Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart' — the verse Jesus calls the greatest commandment. And the warning: when you are full, do not forget.
stops.after: Blessings, curses, a song, and a grave no one has found.

stops.before: The covenant is renewed with blessings and curses laid out like two roads. Moses has one mountain left to climb.
stops.watch: 'I have set before you life and death… choose therefore life.' The song of Moses, the blessing of the tribes, and then Nebo: God shows him the whole land and buries him himself. 'There arose no more a prophet in Israel like unto Moses' — until, the Gospels will say, one greater.
stops.after: Joshua stands at the Jordan with the promise in his hands.
